title: Eating Chili Peppers May Raise the Risk of One Cancer
hook: A major review found heavy chili-pepper eaters had a substantially higher risk of esophageal cancer — though it's an association, not proof, and the picture is murkier for other cancers.
key_points: A major review found the heaviest chili-pepper consumers had notably higher esophageal cancer risk.
Evidence was less clear for stomach and colorectal cancers.
The findings show an association, not proof that chili peppers cause cancer.
Researchers say more research is needed to know if moderate consumption carries similar risk.
content_html: Chili peppers are a dietary staple for a huge share of the world's population, which is part of why a new review of the evidence on chili peppers and cancer risk is getting attention.
extra_html:
As ScienceDaily reports, the review found that people who consumed the most chili peppers had a substantially higher risk of esophageal cancer compared to those who ate little or none. The evidence was murkier for stomach and colorectal cancers, where the pattern was weaker or inconsistent across studies.

Researchers are careful to frame this as an association, not proof of cause and effect — the studies reviewed are largely observational, so other dietary or lifestyle differences between heavy chili eaters and everyone else could be playing a role. It's also not yet clear whether the risk applies mainly to very heavy, frequent consumption or extends to more moderate amounts. The honest takeaway for now is "worth more research," not "stop eating spicy food."

related.title: Cancer Screenings Worth Knowing
related.hook: Screening looks for cancer before symptoms start — and for a few common cancers, that early catch dramatically improves the odds.
